article.articleHeadline: How did a comedian die after a tonsillectomy? A postoperative infection triggered the tragedy.
article.articleSummary: On November 7, A Yan, a signed actor with Dalian Hui Xiao Comedy and a Tencent ‘Single-rank Comedy Contest’ participant, died after a tonsillectomy due to a postoperative infection. article.articleHeadline: Molecular Survey Detects Widespread Zoonotic Parasites in Hubei Goat Herds
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-11-12, across five goat-farming regions in Hubei Province, China, a cross-sectional molecular survey of 500 fecal samples (April 2024–April 2025) found widespread circulation of Giardia duodenalis (29.4%), Enterocytozoon bieneusi (16.2%), and Cryptosporidium spp. (3.2%). This provides the province’s first molecular baseline for these pathogens. Cryptosporidium positives (n=16) were mainly C. bovis (8) and C. xiaoi (6); zoonotic lineages included C. parvum IIdA19G1 and C. ubiquitum XIIa (one each, 6.3% of positives). Giardia and E. bieneusi harbored human-infective lineages as well, indicating cross-species transmission potential. Regionally, prevalence varied (e.g., Xiangyang 6.9%). Molecular work used nested PCR targeting multi-locus loci for Giardia, ITS for E. bieneusi, SSU rRNA and gp60 for Cryptosporidium, with BLAST and phylogenetic validation. Goats thus represent reservoirs with public-health implications.

article.articleHeadline: World Pneumonia Day: Prevent Pneumonia, Don't Miss This "Hidden Variant" of Pertussis
article.articleSummary: World Pneumonia Day (Nov 12) underscores pneumonia as a leading killer of children under five, while warning of a hidden variant: pertussis (Bordetella pertussis) as a major contributor to severe pneumonia in infants. In China, pertussis cases surged to over 470,000 in 2024, about 12-fold the previous year, marking a 40-year outbreak peak for this statutory infectious disease. Pertussis is highly transmissible (R0 12–17), with infants—especially those under 2 months—at greatest risk, and about 60% of cases co-infected with other pathogens, worsening outcomes. Paroxysmal cough can persist for weeks to months, and infections occur in older children and adults who can unknowingly transmit to babies. Vaccination is emphasized: China plans to adjust the DTaP schedule to 2,4,6,18 months and 6 years from 2025, and has introduced a three-component pertussis vaccine (PT, FHA, PRN) for 2 months and above to boost protection.

article.articleHeadline: Monkeypox — 26-year-old man with genital rash; during the incubation period, he met a man on a social platform and had high-risk exposure.
article.articleSummary: 26-year-old man in Hong Kong diagnosed with monkeypox after high-risk contact with a man met via social media during the incubation period. Genital, hand, and facial rashes developed, followed by fever; admitted to Tseung Kwan O Hospital for isolation. Laboratory testing confirmed monkeypox. Epidemiological investigation ongoing; case will be reported to WHO. Since 2022, Hong Kong has recorded 119 monkeypox cases, 94 locally acquired, all male. From August, 26 cases: all reported high-risk sexual activity with men or multiple partners during incubation, most had not received monkeypox vaccination. Local patients frequently used dating apps to find male partners; some could not be traced post-diagnosis, hampering contact tracing. Public health measures include intensified monkeypox prevention messaging on social media and collaboration with dating app operators to push prevention and vaccination information to Hong Kong users.

article.articleHeadline: Magnetic Beads and Digital PCR Detect Bloodstream Pathogens in Three Hours
article.articleSummary: Researchers from Jilin University and affiliated hospitals in Changchun, China report a rapid bloodstream pathogen assay that combines amino-functionalized silica-coated magnetic beads (MBs@SiO2-NH2) with multiplex droplet digital PCR to identify four organisms within three hours. The assay targets Staphylococcus aureus, Enterococcus faecalis, Escherichia coli, and Klebsiella pneumoniae, with a limit of detection of 10 CFU/mL in spiked blood. It uses non-specific electrostatic capture by positively charged bead surfaces, followed by single-well absolute nucleic acid quantification, bypassing culture enrichment and producing quantitative data without external calibration curves. Magnetic enrichment efficiencies are 96.4% for S. aureus, 94.9% for E. coli, 95.4% for E. faecalis, and 94.8% for K. pneumoniae, applicable to both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. In the clinical context, bloodstream infections drive sepsis morbidity and mortality; delays in targeted therapy increase mortality (~7.6% per hour). Standard cultures require 12–48 hours.

article.articleHeadline: Marine Pathogen Vibrio splendidus Employs Mcp14320 Receptor for Targeted
article.articleSummary: Vibrio splendidus AJ01 uses Mcp14320, a TarH-type four-helix bundle chemoreceptor, to navigate toward L-aspartate. Identified by Ningbo University researchers and published in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology, Mcp14320 corresponds to a 1992 bp open reading frame (GenBank PZ511496). Domain analysis reveals TarH ligand-binding domain, two transmembrane regions, HAMP, and methyl-accepting domains; SWISS-MODEL supports a four-helix bundle fold and HMMER confirms TarH motifs. Phylogenetically, Mcp14320 clusters with Tar receptors from E. coli and Salmonella, distinct from dCache-type receptors like Vibrio cholerae Mlp24 and MCP4580. Deletion of mcp14320 (AJ01/Δmcp14320) leaves growth in 2216E broth over 48 h, and swimming/swarming motility unchanged, but eliminates chemotaxis toward L-aspartate in capillary assays across 20 canonical amino acids. Vibrio splendidus is a marine, Gram-negative opportunistic aquaculture pathogen affecting Manila clam Ruditapes philippinarum, triggering hepatopancreas immune/metabolic disruption. This work clarifies a marine TarH-type chemoreceptor's role in nutrient sensing.

article.articleHeadline: A carpet-like brain lesion looked like a tumor -- but pathology revealed a rare form of tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: 67-year-old woman from Changchun, northeastern China, presented with two weeks of progressive left‑leg weakness and speech difficulty. Brain MRI showed a carpet‑like mass attached to the dura; neurosurgeons at the First Hospital of Jilin University removed it completely. Pathology diagnosed tuberculoma, a brain tuberculosis lesion, reported by Xiaodong Yu, Pu Gao and Ning Xu in the Journal of Craniofacial Surgery (online Dec 26, 2025). This dural en plaque–like tuberculoma is exceptionally rare and often mimics en plaque meningioma; imaging clues (tuberculomas tend to be dark on T2) aid but histology remains definitive. Postoperative anti-tuberculosis therapy was started after a week. CNS tuberculosis is uncommon, with dural tuberculomas described in only a handful of cases since 1927. Globally, WHO cites 2024 TB: 10.7 million illnesses and 1.23 million deaths; US 2025 provisional TB cases ~10,260 (3.0/100,000), down slightly from 2024, with higher incidence in adults ≥65.

article.articleHeadline: Avian Influenza Hemagglutinin Mutation Hotspots Drive Cross-Species Spread
article.articleSummary: Avian influenza A(H9N2) hemagglutinin mutation hotspots drive cross-species spread; as of 2026-11-12, the virus has circulated globally since its 1966 Wisconsin detection, with endemic poultry populations and serving as a reservoir for internal gene segments to H5N1 and H7N9, and exhibiting antibody evasion and environmental thermostability. A study analyzing 13,984 full-length HA sequences from domestic birds, wild birds, humans, and swine found 179 highly variable positions (entropy ≥0.2), with HA168 and HA145 among the most diverse. Cross-species hotspot profiles are highly similar between avian and human isolates (Pearson r=0.99); wild-bird isolates are less similar (r=0.77). Residue 145 is serine in wild birds but aspartic acid in poultry/humans; residue 168 is serine in wild birds, with alanine in poultry and both alanine/asparagine in humans, indicating domestic poultry as a transitional reservoir. Researchers built a deep mutational scanning library targeting 179 hotspot sites in HA from A/chicken/Beijing/16/2013 to map mutational effects beyond traditional surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: Avian Influenza Hemagglutinin Mutation Hotspots Drive Cross-Species Spread
triage.triage_reason: Multiple highly pathogenic avian influenza subtypes (H5N1, H7N9, H9N2, H5N8) with documented cross-species transmission potential and global circulation. triage.notes: The article is primarily research-focused analyzing H9N2 mutation hotspots with a reference strain from Beijing (A/chicken/Beijing/16/2013). While Wisconsin is mentioned as the historical 1966 detection location, the primary subject matter of current circulation and cross-species spread involves China (endemic poultry populations, domestic birds as transitional reservoir). The study demonstrates antibody evasion and environmental thermostability of circulating H9N2, with capability to reassort with H5N1 and H7N9 - all high-consequence pathogens. This represents significant pandemic preparedness concern.

article.articleHeadline: Sinus Tract Presence Associates With Documented Microbiological Positivity
article.articleSummary: Chronic osteomyelitis in Northwest China (Kashi, First People’s Hospital of Kashi) shows sinus tract presence independently associates with higher documented microbiological positivity. In a retrospective cohort of 303 hospital records (2012–2019), documented microbiological positivity (positive PN=1) occurred in 214 cases (70.6%). Adjusted analyses reveal sinus tract presence → adjusted prevalence ratio 1.82 (95% CI 1.30–2.54; P<0.001). Standardized adjusted probabilities: 76.5% with sinus tract vs 44.8% without, an adjusted difference of 31.8 percentage points (bootstrap 95% CI 16.0–47.5). Among positives, Staphylococcus aureus (including MRSA) comprised 134/214 (62.6%); at least one Gram-negative organism in 75/214 (35.0%), with Escherichia coli 11.2% and Pseudomonas aeruginosa 9.8%; polymicrobial infections in 30 cases (14.0%). In traumatic osteomyelitis, open injury was not independently associated (PR 1.10, 95% CI 0.91–1.32). Limitations include lack of data on specimen source or sampling intensity; sinus-tract specimens are not validated substitutes for deep bone/operative sampling.

article.articleHeadline: The Russian ambassador to Mongolia: Russia is ready to help Mongolia in the fight against animal infections.
article.articleSummary: Russia is ready to help Mongolia fight animal infections as livestock cases rise 4.4-fold in nine months, the Russian ambassador to Mongolia told reporters in Ulaanbaatar on 12 November 2026. Mongolia, aiming to boost meat imports from Russia, is expanding its foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) response with Russian and Chinese laboratories to produce a domestic vaccine after a SAT-1 outbreak. Mongolia signed a 12 June 2026 contract with Russia for vaccine procurement. The first dose reached about 2.3 million animals in border aimags Bayan-Ölgii, Khovd, Govi-Altai, Uvs and Zavkhan; the August outbreak had ended at that point. By late October, roughly 5 million head across 13 aimags had been vaccinated, with 3.6 million additional doses purchased for a third prophylaxis phase. Vaccination in central and gobi regions is planned to finish by 1 December 2026. FMD is a highly contagious viral disease of cloven-hoofed animals; transmission can be via aerosols and humans can be infected through raw milk; Mongolia had not seen FMD since the 1960s, reappearing in 2000, with serotypes O and A most common.

article.articleHeadline: One-pot CRISPR assay accurately detects white spot syndrome virus in shrimp
article.articleSummary: One-pot OAERA-Cas12a assay detects white spot syndrome virus (WSSV) in shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei). Developed to streamline diagnostics in shrimp aquaculture where WSSV poses an ongoing threat and qPCR requires lab infrastructure. The assay combines asymmetric enzymatic recombinase amplification with CRISPR/Cas12a in a single reaction. Optimal conditions: 46 °C, 1:120 primer ratio, 1 µM Cas12a, Cas12a:crRNA 4:1. Specificity showed no cross-reactivity with non-target shrimp pathogens. Sensitivity with plasmid standards: LOD ~10 copies/µL, 24/25 positives (96%; 95% CI 79.7–99.9%). At 50 copies/µL: 25/25 positives. Visual readout within 15 minutes. In 57 farm/submission samples tested against qPCR, all matched: 9/9 positives and 48/48 negatives (100% agreement; 95% CI 93.7–100%). Authors: Ma, Liu, Zhou (Ningbo University) with Pan (Zhejiang SUPCON), Hangzhou, China. Published in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology, 2026; field validation pending.

article.articleHeadline: One in eight is due to infections.
article.articleSummary: An analysis by WHO and IARC, published in Lancet Oncology, finds infections linked to about 2.3 million new cancers in 2024, 12% of global cases. Five infections dominate: Helicobacter pylori ~760,000 cases (4%), mainly non-cardia gastric cancer; HPV ~750,000 (4%), mainly cervical cancer; HBV ~360,000 (2%); EBV ~260,000 (1%), chiefly lymphomas and nasopharyngeal carcinoma; HCV ~160,000 (<1%), with hepatocellular carcinoma as the main presentation. Viruses act via three routes: disabling tumor suppressors, integrating into host DNA, or carrying oncogenes; bacteria via chronic inflammation (H. pylori). Preventive tools—HPV and HBV vaccines, HCV antivirals, HBV treatment with tenofovir, and H. pylori eradication—lower cancer risk (gastric cancer incidence by 36%, mortality by 22%). Australia’s HPV vaccination since 2007, 83% coverage, and projected elimination of cervical cancer by 2035. East Asia 990,000 cases (42%); Sub-Saharan Africa bears the highest proportional burden (~25%); 77% of infection-related cancers occur in low- and middle-income countries.

article.articleHeadline: A 39-year-old Beijing-based male celebrity agent dies suddenly, leaving the internet in shock: Is COVID-19 back?
article.articleSummary: Beijing-based 39-year-old celebrity agent Hao Boyan died on Nov 9, 2026 in Beijing after prolonged illness diagnosed as COVID-19. He initially had fever and cough treated at home, but deteriorated to COVID-19 pneumonia with lung damage, perforation, systemic dysbiosis, GI bleeding and multi-organ injury despite hospital care; death attributed to cytokine storm. This case shows SARS-CoV-2 remains circulating in a post-pandemic era. In 2026, July recorded 522,000 new infections (6.61× June); September in Sichuan province alone exceeded 9,000 new infections, with rising hospital admissions. Macau travelers’ family cases included Coxsackievirus and COVID-19; others, including a Hunan TV host, also contracted COVID-19. Leeds University researchers link rising autoimmune diseases to prior infection; post-COVID risks include myocarditis, myocardial infarction, stroke, and immune fatigue. Prevention: wear masks in crowds, ventilate, avoid heavy exertion during the infection window, and seek care if fever lasts >3 days; emphasize long-term health and coexistence with the virus.

article.articleHeadline: Novel Regimen Raises Treatment Success for Retreated Pulmonary Tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: Retreated drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis in China: a prospective multicenter observational cohort of 584 patients from 31 designated TB hospitals (2009–2021) shows that a novel regimen, 4HL2EZS(Lfx)/4HL2E (rifapentine twice weekly with levofloxacin replacing streptomycin), improves outcomes over standard retreatment regimens 2HREZS/6HRE or 3HREZ/6HRE. Adjusted odds of treatment success were higher with the novel regimen (aOR 1.988; 95% CI 1.307–3.024; p=0.001), while treatment failure was markedly lower (aOR 0.153; 95% CI 0.072–0.325; p<0.001). Sputum culture conversion at 2 months and loss to follow-up were similar between groups. Long-term recurrence was lower with the experimental regimen; control group had higher odds of recurrence (aOR 5.512; 95% CI 1.602–18.970; p=0.007), though only 13 recurrences occurred, yielding a wide CI. Kaplan–Meier analysis favored the novel regimen, with no increase in adverse events.

article.articleHeadline: Malnutrition in elderly patients with pulmonary tuberculosis: a systematic
article.articleSummary: Pulmonary tuberculosis in older adults shows high concurrent malnutrition: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 15 studies (n=5,346, age ≥60) finds a pooled malnutrition prevalence of 38.8% (95% CI 30.5–47.9). The work, led by researchers in Chongqing, China, synthesizes evidence from cross-sectional, cohort, and case-control designs across multiple clinical settings. Using GLIM criteria, with a three-tier diagnostic approach, the authors distinguish full GLIM implementations (phenotypic plus etiologic indicators) from GLIM-compatible low-BMI and Mini Nutritional Assessment-based methods; twelve GLIM studies yield a prevalence of 39.2% (CI 31.3–47.7%), while three MNA studies yield 37.9%. Significant heterogeneity (I2=96.4%; 95% PI 13.2–72.6). The study notes malnutrition worsens immune dysfunction, prolongs hospitalization, increases treatment failure and mortality, and emphasizes consistent diagnostic criteria. Data drawn from PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, CNKI, and Wanfang through 18 Sep 2026; published in Frontiers in Nutrition.

article.articleHeadline: Pediatric Bronchiolitis Study Analyzes Respiratory Pathogens and Hospital
article.articleSummary: Hebei Children’s Hospital, Shijiazhuang, northern China, conducted a retrospective study of 132 infants (≤2 years) with acute bronchiolitis admitted Sept 2022–Feb 2025. Using a 13-pathogen multiplex RT-PCR panel, 112 children were tested within 24 hours of admission; overall pathogen detection was 88.4% (99/112). Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human rhinovirus were the predominant infectious drivers. Among those tested, single-pathogen infections occurred in 77 cases (68.8%), while multi-pathogen infections occurred in 22 cases (19.6%); 13 children (11.6%) fell into an additional category due to data limitations. The cohort had a male predominance (male:female 2.3:1), median age 6.6 months, with 46.2% under six months. The median hospital length of stay was 6 days. No specific viral profile or polymicrobial infection significantly extended hospitalization. Specimens were collected within 24 hours, with quality controls and acknowledgment that nucleic acid detection does not prove active disease.

article.articleHeadline: Urogenital Neisseria meningitidis in China Shares Global Lineages and Drug
article.articleSummary: Urogenital Neisseria meningitidis lineages circulating in China (Shanghai and Guangzhou) — notably ST-1466 and ST-11,026 — share close genetic ties with international strains and harbor antimicrobial resistance determinants. In 14 isolates (10 urogenital, 4 pharyngeal) from gonorrhea high-risk populations, antimicrobial susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequencing with phylogenetic and pan-genome analyses revealed ST-1466 (six isolates) clustering with the North American Cluster B but with resistance profiles resembling Cluster A, while ST-11,026 Chinese and Japanese isolates formed a tight cluster with ciprofloxacin resistance. ST-3200 aligned with other Chinese isolates. Most isolates were resistant to penicillin and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole; one pharyngeal isolate showed reduced susceptibility to third-generation cephalosporins and carried the pen842 allele. Recombination in iron acquisition and metabolic loci suggests diversification. Authors call for strengthened genomic surveillance and routine susceptibility testing for Neisseria meningitidis from urogenital infections. Published Nov 10, 2026; current date 2026-11-12.

article.articleHeadline: Hospital Study Traces Influenza A Shifts and Diagnostic Biases Across
article.articleSummary: Influenza A testing at the Third Hospital of Mianyang in Southwest China shows stage-dependent shifts across three periods: pre-pandemic baseline, COVID-19 containment, and post-pandemic recovery. Analyzing 57,704 respiratory tests from Oct 26, 2018 to Jul 11, 2024, influenza A positivity averaged 14.8% (Stage 1 pre-pandemic 13.0%; Stage 2 containment 4.5%; Stage 3 post-pandemic 17.8%). The stage boundary was Dec 19, 2022 (post-breakpoint Dec 20, 2022). Caveats: hospital-based percentages reflect testing volume, triage criteria, and assay changes, not community transmission. Monthly testing rose from ~670 in Stage 1 to ~270 in Stage 2, then ~2,000 in Stage 3, creating spectrum bias during Stage 2. Diagnostic platforms evolved: Stage 1–2 used rapid colloidal gold immunoassays (One Step Influenza A and B, Guangzhou Wondfo); Stage 3 introduced real-time PCR (Sansure Biotech), with 17,735 PCR and 20,408 colloidal gold tests among 38,143 Stage 3 tests (46.5% PCR).

article.articleHeadline: USP develops biodegradable packaging with silver that combats bacteria in the laboratory, while tests with nanoparticles record up to 90.7% reduction in E. coli.
article.articleSummary: Researchers at the University of São Paulo (USP) and Peruvian scientists developed a biodegradable film from chitosan, vanillin, and silver nanoparticles with antibacterial activity. In antimicrobial assays, silver nanoparticles reduced Escherichia coli viability by 88.4%–90.7% after three hours; Staphylococcus aureus reductions reached 71.5% after 24 hours. Direct contact with the films demonstrated effects varying by organism and exposure time. Vanillin increased tensile strength from 38 to 48 MPa, while silver nanoparticles slowed moisture transmission by up to 17.4 hours. Antioxidant activity rose four- to sevenfold, and UV blocking occurred with silver. Human cell viability stayed above 70% at nanoparticle concentrations up to 12 µg/mL. In soil, pure chitosan degraded in ~20 days; chitosan-vanillin reached 87.7% degradation by day 30, whereas silver-containing films degraded more slowly, challenging industrial deployment. Not yet approved for foods; studies on silver migration, real-fruit/vegetable performance, and scalability are ongoing. Published in ACS Food Science & Technology.

article.articleHeadline: US, Mexico and Guatemala May Lose Measles-Free Status
article.articleSummary: An independent PAHO Regional Monitoring and Verification Commission is meeting in Washington to decide whether the United States, Mexico, and Guatemala retain measles elimination status as cases surge across the Americas. The panel reviews 2025 data and the first half of 2026 amid a sharp measles resurgence, including the largest and deadliest US outbreak in nearly 30 years. PAHO reported 57,666 confirmed measles cases across 17 countries/territories in January–October 2026. Under PAHO criteria, status is lost if the same measles virus strain circulates uninterrupted for 12 months; investigators use genetic sequencing and assess vaccination coverage, surveillance, and outbreak response. Recommendations go to PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa for final determination, with an official announcement expected early next week. Officials caution the US is likely to lose elimination status, which would prompt renewed public-health efforts; Brazil’s 2024 regain is cited as context.

article.articleHeadline: Mass Rabies Vaccination in Indigenous Territory Faces Logistical and
article.articleSummary: Mass rabies vaccination in the Maxakali Indigenous Territory of northeastern Minas Gerais, Brazil followed a Desmodus rotundus bat-borne outbreak in April–May 2022 that killed four children aged 4–12. An emergency campaign immunized 553 domestic animals: 427 dogs (77.2%) and 126 cats (22.8%). Vaccination by village: Água Boa 276 (49.9%), Cachoeirinha and Escola Floresta 122 (22.1%), Pradinho 98 (17.7%), Verde 57 (10.3%). Human vaccination reached 99.8% first-dose coverage across affected villages, but animal containment required separate veterinary operations and logistics. Lack of baseline animal denominators prevented precise coverage estimates and hindered transmission interruption. The One Health approach integrated human, animal, and environmental health, but highlighted infrastructural, intercultural, and logistical barriers to sustained rabies control in remote Indigenous settlements. Global Zero by 30 guidelines suggest 60–80% canine vaccination thresholds, which field activity approached in accessible animals yet remained imprecise due to census gaps.

article.articleHeadline: Salvage of host-derived geranylgeraniol limits fosmidomycin efficacy in murine Plasmodium berghei malaria
article.articleSummary: Host-derived geranylgeraniol salvage limits fosmidomycin efficacy in a murine Plasmodium berghei malaria model. The work draws a multinational collaboration across institutions in Brazil (University of São Paulo), the United States (Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia), and Europe (ISGlobal/Barcelona and other partners), highlighting mechanistic investigation of drug response in a murine malaria model. The article reports no human cases or outbreaks, focusing on experimental findings to understand factors influencing fosmidomycin efficacy and potential resistance pathways in P. berghei.

article.articleHeadline: Fecal Bacteria Fail to Predict Persistent Protozoan Parasites in Brazilian
article.articleSummary: Giardia species and Cystoisospora species DNA persisted in southern Brazil’s Pelotas microregion (Rio Grande do Sul) across eight sites and four campaigns (Mar–Aug 2025) along urban drainage canals, receiving waters, a drinking-water reservoir, and a Patos Lagoon beach (Praia do Laranjal). Conventional fecal indicator E. coli showed strong temporal dynamics: high in dry periods (>300 CFU/100 mL) and near-zero by August (<1–4 CFU/100 mL), with E. coli negatively correlated with rainfall (rho −0.47) and positively with temperature (rho 0.73). In contrast, protozoan genetic markers did not mirror bacterial declines, remaining detectable despite rising turbidity (0.46–0.63 NTU) and cooler temperatures (13.5–21.1°C). Two-liter sample concentration and molecular screening revealed persistent parasite DNA across urban drainage networks and receiving waters, indicating substantial blind spots in monitoring approaches that rely on culturable E. coli and underscoring ongoing exposure risks in drinking-water, irrigation, and recreational contexts in southern Brazil.

article.articleHeadline: Critical discovery against a parasite that destroys the heart muscle: The infection cycle of Chagas disease has been broken.
article.articleSummary: Chagas disease, a neglected tropical infection threatening about 8 million people worldwide and capable of causing lethal cardiomyopathy, could be halted by targeting the Trypanosoma cruzi IP6K protein. Brazilian researchers from the University of São Paulo and collaborators report in Communications Biology that disabling both copies of the IP6K gene or reducing IP6K production prevents parasite persistence in human heart cells. Parasites with reduced IP6K fail to progress to the infectious blood form, curtailing intra-host spread. Structural analysis shows only ~25% similarity between parasite IP6K and human proteins, suggesting a favorable safety margin for targeted drugs. Brazil's Chagas burden includes acute infection transmitted by triatomine kissing bugs and progression to chronic cardiac and digestive disease, with about 30% mortality from heart failure and 10% severe digestive complications. The team also explored IP6K effects on Leishmania, hinting at broader tropical-disease applications. Current 50-year-old therapies remain problematic.

article.articleHeadline: A fungus that can survive in soil for up to 30 years has already forced farmers to cut down banana plantations in South America and threatens the Prata and Nanica varieties in Brazil, which is trying to prevent its entry.
article.articleSummary: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense race 4 tropical (Foc R4T) is a soil-borne fungus capable of persisting in soil for up to 30 years via chlamydospores and has already forced South American banana farmers to uproot plants. It infects through secondary roots, blocks the plant’s water/nutrient transport, and can kill entire banana stands. Brazil classifies Foc R4T as a quarantine pest absent so far, but warns that over 90% of Brazilian banana varieties are highly susceptible, including Prata and Nanica. In 2025 Brazil produced 7,288,960 tonnes over 471,439 hectares, valued at about R$16.4 billion, with São Paulo leading. Confirmed outbreaks occurred in Colombia (2019) and Peru (2021); Venezuela’s Renacer community in Aragua has faced infections since 2023, prompting uprooting of bananas and a shift to maize, aided by FAO support for diversification. Brazil’s defense focuses on preventing entry and rapid detection, with a national prevention and surveillance plan updated since 2020 and lab-based confirmation for diagnosis.

article.articleHeadline: Rocky Mountain spotted fever concerns after deaths in Espírito Santo.
article.articleSummary: Rocky Mountain spotted fever concerns arise in Espírito Santo, Brazil, after a 73-year-old man in Mimoso do Sul with suspected RMSF had blood sent to Lacen-ES for confirmation. A Nov 7 municipal bulletin shows 69 disease notifications in Mimoso do Sul, with 3 confirmed cases and 24 under investigation; among confirmed, two deaths: a 12-year-old girl in July and a woman in April. RMSF is a tick-borne infection caused by Rickettsia bacteria. In Brazil, Rickettsia rickettsii causes Brazilian RMSF (more severe), reported mainly in northern Paraná and the Southeast; Rickettsia parkeri occurs in Atlantic Forest areas (Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, Bahia, Ceará) and tends to be milder. Common symptoms include fever, severe headache, myalgias, nausea/vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain; a non-pruritic rash often starts on wrists/ankles and can spread to palms/soles. Diagnosis is challenging early; tests include IFA, immunohistochemistry, PCR, and culture, but treatment should begin on clinical suspicion and is free via SUS, typically seven days, with three additional days after fever ends. Prevention focuses on avoiding tick exposure; if a tick is found, remove with tweezers and wash the area.

triage.headline_ja: エスピリトサント州での死亡後、ロッキー山紅斑熱（紅斑熱群リケッチア症）への懸念
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル・エスピリトサント州の一自治体（Mimoso do Sul）で紅斑熱（RMSF）による死亡例が報告されているが、ダニ媒介性でヒト-ヒト感染はなく、国際的拡大の可能性は低い。地域の風土病的側面が強く、PICKUP基準には届かないが死亡例の推移を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Corguinho Reports 19 Positive Cases of Human Leishmaniasis, but SES Confirms Six; Understand the Difference.
article.articleSummary: In Corguinho, a divergence between municipal and state health authorities over leishmaniasis figures highlights diagnostic criteria differences. The Municipal Health Department reports 19 positive results among 38 evaluated for Leishmaniasis tegumentary americana (LTA), with 18 negatives and one case under investigation, based on clinical assessments. In contrast, the State Health Secretariat (SES) confirms six new laboratory-confirmed LTA cases in 2026, plus one recurrence, drawn from SINAN; this matches the total new diagnoses recorded in all of 2025. The discrepancy stems from SES reporting only lab-confirmed cases, while the municipality includes suspected/undetermined cases undergoing treatment. No deaths reported; four cases cured; others ongoing. Cases are predominantly in rural Corguinho, ages 35–84 (four men, two women). Transmission via sand flies; environmental factors include deforestation and proximity to wooded areas. Prevention includes repellents, screens, nets, and yard cleaning; SES notes municipality rapid tests target canine visceral leishmaniasis and may not indicate human LTA.

triage.notes: リーシュマニア症はブラジル農村部での風土病であり、サシチョウバエ媒介、ヒト-ヒト感染なし。死亡者なし、4件治癒済み。地方自治体レベルの報告基準の相違が主題であり、公衆衛生上の緊急性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Ver-o-Peso açaí boxes undergo inspection after cases of Chagas disease in Belém.
article.articleSummary: Belém, Pará, Brazil—The Ver-o-Peso açai sector underwent a 'Açaí Safe' inspection by the Belém City Health Secretariat (Sesma), Sanitary Surveillance Department (Devisa) and Casa do Açaí on 12 November 2026. Ten açai boxes were inspected; samples were collected for microbiological and microscopic analysis at Lacen, with results expected in about 15 days. The operation addresses hygiene conditions and risks of diseases transmitted by contaminated products, notably Chagas disease. If deficiencies are identified, vendors will be notified and advised on corrective actions. In addition, free training with certification for Ver-o-Peso workers will be offered; Casa do Açaí has trained about 2,500 beaters; sessions run Tuesdays and Thursdays, 14:00–18:00, focusing on safe preparation. Expanding to Mosqueiro, Outeiro and Cotijuba; more than 100 açai samples have been collected citywide, and licensing guidance is provided.

article.articleHeadline: The WHO deploys new mobile laboratories for viral alert in Africa | HSB Noticias
article.articleSummary: The World Health Organization deploys a network of mobile genomic sequencing laboratories across East and Central Africa to detect infectious mutations in real time and accelerate preventive vaccine delivery in vulnerable border zones. The portable infrastructure lets epidemiology teams process biological samples on site and obtain results in under 24 hours, avoiding shipment to reference centers in Europe or North America. This capacity supports early detection and surveillance of hemorrhagic fever outbreaks and emerging respiratory pathogens, enabling timely containment measures. The program includes training of local technicians and provision of reagents and lab supplies to ensure continuity. Philanthropic organizations have pledged additional funding to explore expanding this surveillance model to the Amazon regions of South America in the coming year.

article.articleHeadline: 15-year-old boy dies, infected by his cousin with a serious STI - Diário do Amapá
article.articleSummary: In Macapá, Amapá, Brazil, a 15-year-old boy, Marcos Vinícius, died on November 11, 2026, in the ICU of the Hospital da Criança e do Adolescente after a severe pulmonary infection aggravated by a sexually transmitted infection contracted during rapes by his 27-year-old cousin. Investigations by the DERCCA show abuse began when he was 11, with the offender living in the same home. The suspect was arrested on November 3 and indicted for rape of a vulnerable person, and remains in custody. Unconfirmed reports suggest the boy may have contracted HIV as a result of the abuse, not officially confirmed by hospital or family. The case has prompted calls for reporting violence against children and adolescents. The body was laid out at a funeral home behind HCAL (Dr. Alberto Lima Clinical Hospital) in central Macapá, with burial at São José Cemetery.

article.articleHeadline: Infectious Diseases 2026
article.articleSummary: Newcastle disease (ND) crisis in Brazil persists with a fifth outbreak confirmed by MAPA. The latest outbreak was detected on a commercial poultry farm in Nova Itaberaba, western Santa Catarina, an area under a declared zoosanitary state of emergency. The evolving sanitary situation is disrupting international trade, including the return of nine shipping containers carrying poultry products destined for West Africa (eight for Ghana, one for Angola) after it was found the products had been processed within the restricted sanitary zone in Santa Catarina, violating trade protocols with the destination countries. The latest outbreak and container incident underscore challenges facing Brazilian poultry exports amid heightened international scrutiny.

article.articleHeadline: Vets warn dog owners: letting their dog's paws stay wet after rain may promote fungal and bacterial infections.
article.articleSummary: Brazilian dogs and cats risk skin lesions and infections from rain moisture trapped between the toes (interdigital spaces). Dry paws with a clean towel after wet walks; for long-haired dogs, a dryer helps remove residual moisture; inspect for redness before allowing activity. Puddles are riskier in summer (Brazilian summer runs Dec 21–Mar 20). Cutaneous mycoses are common; a University of Rio Grande do Sul study found Malassezia pachydermatis in 13.2% of 250 dogs with skin disease, and pododermatitis can be fungal as an opportunist. Standing water can harbor Leptospira bacteria causing leptospirosis in dogs via contact with puddles, floods, or urban runoff; rodent urine is a common source, as is urine from infected dogs. If itching, redness, or behavioral changes persist, seek veterinary care. Boots are generally unnecessary except for protecting existing lesions.

article.articleHeadline: List of COVID-19 Variants from Wuhan Through 2026, Delta Remains the Deadliest
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 SARS-CoV-2 variants traced from Wuhan to 2026 show Delta as the deadliest while Omicron remains the dominant lineage. The original Wuhan strain (late 2019–early 2020) acquired the D614G spike mutation, boosting transmissibility. Alpha (B.1.1.7) emerged in the United Kingdom in 2020 and spread globally, becoming dominant in parts of 2021. Beta (B.1.351), identified in South Africa, carried E484K, raising immune escape concerns. Gamma (P.1) from Brazil in 2020 also had spike mutations associated with higher transmission and reinfection risk. Epsilon (B.1.427/B.1.429) first identified in California; increased spread and reduced neutralization, later surpassed. Lambda (C.37) detected in Peru also raised immune-escape concerns but did not sustain global dominance after Delta and Omicron. Delta (B.1.617.2) from India drove major waves in 2021 with higher severity. By 2026, Omicron subvariants predominate, underscoring ongoing surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola and Insecurity Aggravate the Food Crisis in the Eastern Part of the Country
article.articleSummary: Ebola-related health crisis and persistent insecurity have severely deteriorated food security and rural livelihoods in Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu, according to a FAO assessment (DIEM-Impact) based on 224 informants in Sep 2026, consulted by Radio Okapi on Nov 11, 2026. The Bundibugyo strain of Ebola accelerated by August 2026 to about 500 new cases per week, concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu. North Kivu is hardest hit, with around 1.9 million people already in need of humanitarian assistance before the outbreak. From Jan 2024–Mar 2026, violence restricted access to farmland and livestock theft rose from 15% to 28%. High living costs in Bunia, Bukavu, and Goma reflect trade barriers and transport costs. FAO calls for stronger emergency humanitarian support and targeted agricultural and livestock assistance in the most vulnerable territories: Irumu and Aru (Ituri); Masisi and Rutshuru (North Kivu); Kalehe (South Kivu).

article.articleHeadline: Infection Outbreak Triggers Level 2 CDC Travel Alert
article.articleSummary: Yellow fever outbreak in West Africa prompts the CDC to issue a Level 2 Travel Health Notice for Burkina Faso's Nando, Côte d'Ivoire's Bounkani, and Ghana's Upper West. As of Oct 12, 2026, WHO reports 67 confirmed cases and 18 deaths across nine African countries: Côte d'Ivoire (30 cases, 10 deaths), Burkina Faso (15 cases, 3 deaths), Ghana (4 cases, 3 deaths), Liberia (1 case), Cameroon (9 cases, 1 death), Nigeria (4 cases, 1 death), Central African Republic (2 cases), Guinea (1 case), Togo (1 case). Transmission is mosquito-borne; typical symptoms appear 3-6 days after infection. About 15% progress to severe illness with liver damage, jaundice, bleeding, shock, and organ failure. CDC urges vaccination at least 10 days before travel and mosquito-bite precautions; boosters may be considered for those last vaccinated 10+ years ago in high-risk settings. Vaccination access varies by clinic; certain groups should consult a clinician.

article.articleHeadline: ScienceNet - Mysterious anthrax outbreak among African hippos raises concerns about human-to-human transmission.
article.articleSummary: As of September 2026, Virunga National Park in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo reports an anthrax outbreak among hippos, with at least 30 dead. Laboratory confirmation identifies Bacillus anthracis as the cause. No human infections have been reported yet; authorities are closely monitoring amid concurrent Ebola and cholera outbreaks and ongoing humanitarian crises from conflict. Park teams are monitoring carcass disposal, and there have been no new hippo deaths in the past two weeks. Anthrax spores persist in soil for years; heavy rainfall and river systems can mobilize spores, increasing exposure as hippos graze near contaminated sites. Early antibiotic treatment is effective, but delays can be fatal. Public risk includes handling infected carcasses or consuming contaminated meat; underreporting due to care seeking outside national surveillance is a concern. Livestock vaccination campaigns are underway but costly. In 2025, about 65 hippos died in DRC; Uganda reported 15 human cases, 2 deaths.

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Journalists Face Rising Attacks Over Ebola Reporting
article.articleSummary: As of 12 November 2026, journalists in the Democratic Republic of Congo reporting on the worsening Ebola outbreak face rising attacks and threats. The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) says reporters and media workers have been assaulted during Ebola awareness campaigns, with some accused of spreading misinformation about the disease. The incidents highlight the dangers of covering a public health emergency and the challenges to accurate health messaging during the Ebola crisis. They also raise serious concerns about press freedom in the Democratic Republic of Congo as journalists strive to inform the public while facing intimidation.

article.articleHeadline: The cholera outbreak is worsening in the Katoyi health zone.
article.articleSummary: Cholera outbreak worsens in Katoyi health zone, Masisi, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, where the epidemic declared in mid-September has reached nearly 400 cases and dozens of deaths. A woman and a child died overnight between Wednesday and Thursday, 12 November, at Mangere health center. At least six health areas are affected (Mangere, Biolo, Kirambo, Kikoma, Mahya among them), with at least 15 cholera deaths in the past six days across the affected localities. Health authorities warn of continued transmission amid insecurity and constrained medical supplies. Seventeen cartons of IV fluids and other inputs have been dispatched, but supplies have been blocked for two weeks at Luke, hampering care. The outbreak extends to Masisi and Walikale, with displaced populations especially at risk; partners are urged to reinforce medicines, fluids, and medical materials to prevent humanitarian deterioration.

article.articleHeadline: Tripura conducts Ebola preparedness mock drill at GB Hospital amid global concern
article.articleSummary: Ebola preparedness drill conducted at GB Hospital, Agartala, Tripura, on November 12, 2026, amid global concern over Ebola outbreaks in Africa, including the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. The mock exercise evaluated early identification of suspected cases, immediate isolation, infection prevention and control, and appropriate clinical management protocols. Participants included doctors, nurses, paramedical staff and personnel from various departments; training covered recognizing Ebola symptoms and strict adherence to isolation procedures. Hospital authorities assessed emergency response readiness and containment facilities to prevent transmission to healthcare workers and others. Dr. Shivabrata Bhattacharjee of Agartala Government Medical College emphasized that Tripura has had no reported Ebola cases to date, but imported infection via travelers cannot be ruled out due to cross-border movement. The exercise aims to strengthen surveillance, prompt detection, and response for potential imported or emerging cases.

article.articleHeadline: Ituri: a handwashing station strike rekindles fear of Ebola (Civil Society) - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Handwashing station on the Komanda-Yedi axis in Irumu territory, Ituri province, northeast DRC, was suspended after a strike by attendants demanding unpaid salaries, sparking fears of Ebola virus disease spread amid the ongoing Ebola threat. The Bunia-based civil society group Force Vive and the Basili chiefdom local youth council have issued an SOS to the provincial government to actively engage the International Organization for Migration (IOM). They seek urgent measures to clear arrears and resume the critical infection-prevention service for users along the Komanda–Yedi corridor. The report notes no Ebola cases; the health risk stems from interrupting a key preventive measure in a context of Ebola transmission potential. The call emphasizes prompt payment of arrears and rapid service restoration to safeguard public health.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola vaccine lessons
article.articleSummary: First Ebola identification in 1976 at Yambuku, DRC, with 318 cases and 88% mortality. Six strains identified: Zaire, Sudan, Bundibugjo, Taï Forest, Reston (NHPs), Bombali (bats). Before 2014, vaccine development stalled by market absence. The 2014 West Africa outbreak (Guinea, Sierra Leone, Liberia; spread to seven others) reached 28,616 cases and 11,325 deaths, prompting sustained investment and push/pull incentives. A recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus vaccine in WHO ring-vaccination trials showed 84% effectiveness against Zaire; Ervebo licensed in 2019 after Gavi's 2016 Advance Purchase Commitment. CEPI founded 2016; 100-day mission proposed 2021. The 2022 Uganda Ebola Sudan outbreak had 164 confirmed/probable cases and 78 deaths; 78 days from outbreak ID to vaccine arrival, 74 days to containment. January 2025 Uganda outbreak: 14 cases, 4 deaths, aided by stockpiled vaccines and investigational treatments. Trials for Marburg vaccines in Rwanda (2024) and Ethiopia (2025) progressed; GMP readiness emphasized for deployment.

article.articleHeadline: East Sumba Regency Government Determined to Eliminate AIDS, TB, and Malaria
article.articleSummary: East Sumba Regency aims to eliminate HIV/AIDS, TB, and Malaria (ATM) through the Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health (RSSH) ATM program. A November 11, 2026 cross-sector partnership forum at Padadita Hotel, Waingapu, discussed financing from village/kelurahan budgets and district CSR partners, plus regional support via Adinkes and The Global Fund, to form a local action plan. Attendees included Regent Umbu Lili Pekuwali (represented by Yulius Ngenju) and RSSH ATM coordinator Dr. Hyronimus A. Fernandez, with Bappeda, Health Office, camats, lurahs, and puskesmas staff. HIV/AIDS: 5,010 tested out of a 8,409 target (59.6%); people living with HIV on ART 63.9%. TB: suspects identified 3,187 of 3,558 (89.6%); new case detection 41.3%; treatment success 81.8%. Malaria API 0.84 per 1,000 population (below target <1). TB screening ongoing, but a wide gap remains between suspects examined and confirmed cases.

article.articleHeadline: Two calves in Jembrana, Bali die of rabies.
article.articleSummary: Two calves in Pangyangan village, Pekutatan District, Jembrana, Bali died from rabies, suspected to have been transmitted by stray dogs roaming the area. Reports were received on 27 and 31 October 2026 from farmers. Veterinary officials examined the livestock; one calf displayed classic rabies signs—hypersalivation and aggression—and fled into a river near the farm before dying. Samples were collected and sent to Balai Besar Veteriner (BBVet) for laboratory testing, which confirmed rabies. The infected animals were located within 50–100 meters of each other on the farm. Officials believe transmission likely originated from stray dogs, which could bite multiple animals, enabling spread within the farm. In response, the Bali Agriculture Department initiated surveillance, dog vaccination, community education, and control of stray dog populations to prevent further cases.

article.articleHeadline: Tourists with diarrhea and vomiting after a vacation in Garut, the Health Office struggles to determine the cause.
article.articleSummary: Garut, West Java—The Garut District Health Office (Dinkes) cannot determine the cause of diarrhea and vomiting reported by tourists after visiting Garut. Investigators were deployed, but identifying the source is hindered because visitors ate at multiple venues. Reports surfaced about four days after the incidents, limiting access to food samples or vomitus for testing. Food samples are typically stored for only 24 hours, and none are available for analysis. Officials say the symptoms could stem from a foodborne illness or a viral/bacterial infection from other sources, and a direct link to Garut has not been confirmed. Regardless, Dinkes Garut is using the case to strengthen food-safety oversight and training for tourism-related businesses, including restaurants, hotels, and attractions. The episode drew public attention after social media posts by tourists and local government responses.

article.articleHeadline: FAO warns Asia to brace for emerging diseases, says 75% originate from animals, urges governments to monitor ecosystems under the One Health approach.
article.articleSummary: FAO warns Asia-Pacific to brace for emerging diseases, noting 75% originate from animals and urging One Health-based surveillance that links human, animal, and environmental health. In March Cambodia reported human infections with H5N1 avian influenza; Australia detected H5N1 spread by migratory seabirds, illustrating cross-species risk beyond farms. Climate trends—El Niño expected to peak late 2026—could worsen droughts and heavy rainfall, disrupt livestock production, strain water sources, and raise pandemic risk as farm runoff can carry waste, antimicrobials, and pathogens into water bodies. The FAO proposes three actions: 1) integrate wildlife and environmental data with animal–human disease surveillance to assess risks and guide farm-level prevention; 2) build capacity—training for veterinarians, lab staff, and field personnel and improve cross-sector communication; 3) embed prevention in national plans with clear responsibilities and sustained funding. Thailand, Cambodia, and Indonesia are cited as regional implementation examples.

article.articleHeadline: Disbunnak Kalbar: Biosecurity Key to Controlling African Swine Fever.
article.articleSummary: ASF in West Kalimantan (Kalbar) is driven by biosecurity; first detected Sep 2021 in Kapuas Hulu; spread to 12 districts/cities, excluding Sambas and Kayong Utara. Kalbar pig population fell from 463,570 (2020) to 66,249 (2024) — an 83.48% drop, with estimated economic losses of Rp500–600 billion. In 2023, pork prices reached about Rp190,000 per kg, contributing to inflation. Authorities implemented governor edicts, inter-sector task forces, farmer education, and surveillance, plus disinfection, blood sampling, convalescent serum, and movement controls of live pigs and pork products. Community ASF Biosecurity Intervention (CABI) strengthens biosecurity through two pilot sites: Pontianak City and Landak Regency, now replicated in Singkawang and Sanggau. Pontianak’s area Bukit Rel shows no ASF cases and pig numbers rising. Dinas Kalbar appeals to all pig farmers to maintain biosecurity; support from the Directorate of Animal Health and related agencies is acknowledged.

article.articleHeadline: Malaria Is the Leading Disease in Jayapura City, With 79,000 Residents Screened Positive
article.articleSummary: Malaria remains the leading disease in Jayapura City, Papua, with about 79,000 residents testing positive from over 300,000 screened in 2026. Mass screening covered symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals, driving high positivity in this endemic area. Transmission surveillance targets Muara Tami and Heram districts, where Anopheles mosquitoes sustain spread. Preventive measures include environmental sanitation, bed nets at sleep, and avoiding outdoor night activities without protection. The Health Office intensifies the Find, Treat, and Control (TTM) program via house-to-house early detection. Community-wide screening remains essential, though field access is limited by residents’ farming or fishing schedules. Also noted is low patient compliance in completing malaria regimens, underscoring the need to finish therapy even after symptoms subside. Public health messaging encourages clean-living practices to curb transmission and support maternal/child health improvements.

article.articleHeadline: 39 Gunungkidul residents infected with leptospirosis, 7 dead.
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis in Gunungkidul, Indonesia rose to 39 cases with 7 deaths by end-October 2026, compared with 30 cases and fatalities in 2025. Cases occurred across several kapanewon, including Nglipar, Playen, Ngawen, Gedangsari and Semin. March 2026 recorded the highest transmission, with 15 cases and 3 fatalities; February followed with 10 cases, while other months yielded 1–5 cases. The outbreak's driver is leptospira bacteria shed in rat urine, linking spread to environmental cleanliness alongside dengue-like transmission patterns. Farmers are urged to use personal protective equipment—boots and gloves—and to promptly wash any wounds with soap after fieldwork to reduce exposure. The health department is expanding early-detection capacity and diagnostics to accelerate treatment and curb fatalities, in addition to ongoing community hygiene campaigns.

article.articleHeadline: Surveillance for zoonotic viruses in human population at the human-animal interface in North Sulawesi, Indonesia
article.articleSummary: Surveillance was conducted in Minahasa District, North Sulawesi, Indonesia, as part of the USAID Emerging Pandemic Threats (EPT) PREDICT project, from November 2017 to December 2018, at Noongan Hospital and Puskesmas Kawangkoan. The study targets high risk populations engaging in wildlife hunting, trade and consumption, in a region with documented wildlife related activities and prior reports of potential zoonotic viruses in bats (henipavirus, filovirus, hantavirus). Objectives: establish baseline data on viruses within selected zoonotic families and identify behavioral risk factors for spillover at the human–wildlife interface. Enrollment included syndromic patients aged >2 years presenting with fever (>38 C) for 24 h to 7 days, including SARI, ILI, fever of unknown origin, encephalitis, or hemorrhagic fever. Biological samples collected: oral/nasal, rectal, blood, urine; stored in TRIzol/VTM and shipped to Eijkman Research Center. Molecular detection by RNA extraction and cDNA synthesis followed prior surveillance protocols to detect viruses within zoonotic families.

article.articleHeadline: Delhi Study Finds High Strain Concordance Among Household Contacts of
article.articleSummary: Delhi, India-based prospective cohort study of 134 culture-confirmed rifampicin-resistant or multidrug-resistant TB index cases and 305 household contacts (July 2016–February 2018) found high concordance of drug resistance profiles and genetic strain patterns between index patients and infected household members. Among 19 culture-positive contacts, phenotypic drug susceptibility matched the corresponding index case in 18 pairs (94.7%; 95% CI 74.0–99.9). Spoligotype patterns matched in 18 of 19 pairs (94.7%; 95% CI 74.0–99.9%), with a Cohen’s kappa of 0.89. Baseline testing showed all index cases rifampicin-resistant, 90.3% also resistant to isoniazid, and 41% pre-extensively drug-resistant. Genotyping revealed 14 spoligotype patterns across six major lineages; CAS1_DELHI and Beijing were predominant. Polyclonal infection occurred in 39 of 134 index cases (29.1%). Authors caution spoligotyping’s limited discriminatory power and cannot prove transmission, but findings support systematic household contact investigations for drug-resistant TB.

A Division Bench (Chief Justice Lisa Gill and Justice Challa Gunaranjan) noted the status report was filed by an SI-level officer rather than a DSP-rank officer and faulted the lack of crucial details. Missing information included the tablets’ source, procurement, place and date of manufacture, and the circumstances surrounding the girl’s death. The court also emphasized that no expert medical opinion had been obtained and the deceased’s medical records had not been examined."

article.articleHeadline: During winter, the risk of PPR disease increases in goats; learn its symptoms and prevention.
article.articleSummary: As of 12 November 2026, in Lakhimpur Kheri district, Uttar Pradesh, India, goat winter care warns that Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) poses a major infectious risk as temperatures drop and humidity rises. PPR is a rapidly spreading viral disease among goats, capable of affecting entire herds, especially where many goats are kept together. Symptoms include white nodular lesions on the mouth, gums, and tongue, respiratory distress and pneumonia-like signs, fever, lethargy, reduced appetite, and weakness; severe cases may involve diarrhea and abortion in pregnant goats. Transmission occurs via direct contact with saliva, nasal discharge, and contaminated water, surfaces, or feed, necessitating strict hygiene and isolation of affected animals. There is no specific antiviral treatment; vaccination is the most effective preventive measure. Farmers should arrange timely PPR vaccination through nearby veterinary clinics or officers.

article.articleHeadline: Shigella infection confirmed in 3 areas of Malappuram: How it spreads, symptoms to watch for and who is most at risk
article.articleSummary: Shigella infection confirmed in Malappuram district, Kerala, across Areekode, Pulpatta and Edavanna, reaching eight confirmed cases; additional cases reported in Thiruvananthapuram, Thrissur and Kozhikode as of 2026-11-12. Shigellosis is an intestinal infection caused by Shigella and spreads via the faecal-oral route through contaminated hands, food, water or surfaces; a tiny bacterial dose can cause illness, enabling rapid spread in households, schools and communities with poor sanitation. Symptoms typically appear 1–3 days after exposure and include diarrhoea (sometimes blood or mucus), fever, abdominal cramps, nausea and vomiting; dehydration is a major risk for children. Most recover with oral rehydration; severe cases may require hospitalisation and IV fluids. Antibiotics are not always needed, and resistance exists in some strains, highlighting the need for stool testing before treatment. Prevention focuses on boiled water, thorough handwashing, safe food handling, clean surfaces, and proper waste disposal.

article.articleHeadline: Unified efforts to eradicate filariasis in UP; MDA campaign to run from November 19 to December 5
article.articleSummary: Uttar Pradesh launches a mass drug administration (MDA) campaign under the Sarvajan Dawa Adhiniyam to eradicate filariasis, running from November 19 to December 5. The campaign targets 12.1 million people across 16 districts, spanning 53 blocks (Kanpur Nagar, Unnao, Kanpur Dehat, Chitrakoot, Sitapur, Shahjahanpur, Lakhimpur Kheri, Shravasti, Prayagraj, Gonda, Hardoi, Kannauj, Ballia, Farrukhabad, Fatehpur, Kaushambi). The disease had been present in 782 blocks across 51 districts but is now contained to 53 blocks in 16 districts. A list identifies 1 lakh 91 thousand 487 people who have never taken medicine, 5 lakh 38 thousand 351 migrants, and 3 lakh 31 thousand 368 who refused. The campaign emphasizes door-to-door medication, focus on migrants and refusers, and interdepartmental coordination. Filariasis is spread by infected mosquitoes; untreated infections can lead to elephantiasis and hydrocele.

article.articleHeadline: India Meets WHO TB Death-Reduction Goal Five Years Late, Still Accounts for 23% of Toll | EconoTimes
article.articleSummary: Global TB deaths fell to 1.13 million worldwide in 2025, down from 1.18 million in 2024 and 35% below 2015 levels, per WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 released 12 November 2026. An estimated 10.6 million people developed TB in 2025, including 137,000 deaths among people living with HIV. India achieved the End TB Strategy target of a 35% reduction in TB deaths from 2015 by 2025, five years late, but still accounted for 23% of global TB deaths in 2025. India applied a country-specific model using pandemic-era disruption data and drew on Sample Registration System data not officially submitted to WHO. Bangladesh, China and Viet Nam were noted as other high-burden countries reaching the target outside Africa/Europe. TB care costs remain daunting, with pooled 40-country surveys finding about 47% of treated patients and households facing costs above 20% of annual income; the 2025 global cost estimate was not reported. 2023 UN targets for 2027 call for 90% diagnosis/treatment coverage and 100% initial testing with a rapid diagnostic test.

article.articleHeadline: Telangana government gears up for mega polio drive
article.articleSummary: Telangana will conduct Polio Sunday on November 22 across Hyderabad, Rangareddy, Sangareddy, Medchal-Malkajgiri, and Hanamkonda, vaccinating over 1.8 million children under five with two drops of the bivalent Oral Polio Vaccine at 7,602 booths. A four-day drive includes 245 mobile teams and 245 transit points, overseen by 761 route supervisors and supported by 1,709 ANMs, 5,682 ASHA workers, 5,655 Anganwadi workers, plus volunteers from Mahila Mandalis, MEPMA, SERP, nursing students, and teachers. On November 23–24, house-to-house visits will vaccinate those missed in booths; door-to-door efforts continue in Greater Hyderabad Urban, Rangareddy, Medchal-Malkajgiri, and Sangareddy through November 25. The campaign targets 1,801,698 children and focuses on high-risk zones and migrant families, including urban slums and nomadic communities. Telangana has been polio-free for 18 years; India's last case was in 2007 (Howrah, West Bengal).

article.articleHeadline: Mock drill at Panipat hospital to strengthen Ebola readiness
article.articleSummary: Panipat, Israna: NC Medical College & Hospital conducted a mock drill to bolster Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) preparedness, focusing on early identification, isolation, and transmission prevention. The exercise tested travel history and exposure-based screening, triage, immediate isolation, proper PPE donning/doffing, IPC, biomedical waste management, and safe patient transport via designated routes. It reviewed isolation facilities and essential equipment, and reinforced coordination among Emergency Department, Microbiology, Medicine, Pediatrics, Nursing, Infection Control, and Administration. Training on occupational safety, exposure prevention, reporting to health authorities, and emergency-response roles was emphasized, with a strong aim to prevent hospital-acquired transmission and safeguard patients, staff, and visitors. Dr. Vijay Kumar Dahiya underscored preparedness and timely recognition as cornerstones of Ebola response, while the administration reiterated commitment to readiness per MOHFW and NCDC guidelines. 2026-11-13.

article.articleHeadline: In Lucknow, within 72 hours, three children from the same family died, their health deteriorated one after another after a fever.
article.articleSummary: Three children from the same family died in Malihabad's Khandsara village, Lucknow, within four days after fever. Divyansh, 3, fell ill with mild fever on November 9 around 2:30 pm and died en route to hospital. Kartik, 7, deteriorated the next day and died. Lakshmi, 10, developed fever and abdominal pain on the night of November 10, was admitted to a private hospital, and died on Thursday morning. Postmortems are pending. The third child's blood tests were negative for typhoid, dengue, and malaria; chest X-ray showed severe bilateral pneumonia. Initial suspicion of food poisoning by health officials; the exact cause to be clarified after autopsies. Health authorities, including CMO Dr NB Singh and a team, visited the village; questions were raised about actions after the first two deaths. Investigation ongoing; no confirmed source or imported/exported cases identified.

triage.headline_ja: ラクナウで同一家族の子供3人が72時間以内に死亡、発熱後に体調が次々と悪化

article.articleHeadline: Eight dead, 61 suspected cases in diphtheria cluster
article.articleSummary: Thailand reports 61 suspected diphtheria cases and eight deaths from January 1 to November 9, 2026 (CFR 13%), concentrated in the far south. A regional cluster in three southern provinces and four Songkhla districts accounts for 21 patients and five deaths, with three lab-confirmed; Narathiwat records the most southern cases (10). Ages range 8 months–82 years; median 18; highest infection rate among those under 4; male-to-female ratio 1.14:1. Authorities say there is no nationwide outbreak, but additional cases may emerge where vaccination coverage is low. Actions include intensified surveillance, case finding, contact tracing, and diphtheria antitoxin distribution in high-risk zones, plus collaboration with local authorities and schools to locate unvaccinated children. Diphtheria spreads via respiratory droplets or direct contact; incubation 2–5 days; symptoms fever, sore throat, difficulty swallowing, and a grey throat coating; severe disease can cause airway obstruction, myocarditis, or neurological complications; mortality 5–10%. Vaccination reminders: complete primary series and boosters; check records for catch-up immunization.

triage.headline_ja: ジフテリアクラスターで8人死亡、疑い例61人
triage.triage_reason: タイ南部でジフテリアクラスター（61疑い例、8死亡、CFR13%）が発生し、IHR基準（深刻な公衆衛生影響・異常性）を2つ満たすためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ワクチン未接種の子供を中心に地域的クラスターが発生。低接種率地域での追加症例が懸念されるが、当局は全国的流行ではないとしている。国境地域（ナラティワート）のためマレーシア等への越境リスクは要確認。

article.articleHeadline: Thai Health Ministry revises XDR-TB definition and symptoms
article.articleSummary: Thailand's Ministry of Public Health revised the definition and warning symptoms of extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB), with changes taking effect on November 10, 2026. Published in the Royal Gazette on November 9, 2026 (Notification on the Names and Key Symptoms of Dangerous Communicable Diseases No. 6), XDR-TB is defined as tuberculosis resistant to rifampicin (with or without isoniazid) and to at least one fluoroquinolone (e.g., levofloxacin, moxifloxacin) plus resistance to at least one of bedaquiline or linezolid. Key symptoms include persistent cough, coughing blood, weight loss, loss of appetite, fatigue, fever, chest pain and shortness of breath; severe cases may progress to respiratory failure. The update supports surveillance, prevention and control under the 2015 Communicable Diseases Act, reaffirming XDR-TB as a dangerous infectious disease requiring robust infection-control measures in Thailand.

article.articleHeadline: Winter alert for seven diseases and two health risks from DDC
article.articleSummary: Thailand's Department of Disease Control issued a 2026 winter advisory covering seven infectious diseases and two non-infectious hazards. The diseases: influenza, pneumonia, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, and COVID-19 (respiratory illnesses); acute diarrhoea (food- and waterborne); malaria and scrub typhus (vector-borne). Two health risks: death from cold exposure—exacerbated by alcohol consumption—and carbon monoxide poisoning from poorly ventilated bathrooms with gas water heaters. Precautions focus on vulnerable groups (young children, older adults, people with underlying conditions) and on reducing cold-related risks and indoor hazards: use extractor fans, limit showers to 10 minutes, keep bathroom doors open 15-20 minutes before reuse, seek medical attention for dizziness. For infections: masks in crowds, hand hygiene, vaccination as recommended; eat freshly cooked hot food, drink clean water, use serving spoons. Surveillance by 12 local offices and a rapid-response plan; hotline 1422.

triage.triage_reason: タイ保健当局による季節性疾患への定例的な予防喚起であり、異常な流行や新たな公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示す情報はない。

article.articleHeadline: Thai Medical Council on Nov 12 cites 83% infection-free rate in small weekly dengue pill trial
article.articleSummary: Thai Medical Council on Nov 12 cited 83% infection-free in a small randomized trial of mosnodenvir, an experimental dengue antiviral, as weekly pre-exposure prophylaxis, citing NEJM research. In 2a, four arms (n=6 per arm) included daily dosing, higher- and lower-dose weekly dosing, and placebo; on maintenance day, volunteers were challenged with dengue type 3 and followed 120 days. Five of six in each weekly-dose group were infection-free (no detectable viral RNA or dengue antibodies); four of six in daily-dose, and all six placebo recipients were infected. Mosnodenvir concentrations rose after a loading, and there were no safety concerns. The drug targets NS3-NS4B to block viral RNA replication; preclinical work suggested activity against all four serotypes, but this trial tested protection against type 3. NS4B mutations were observed in breakthrough infections; larger field studies are needed. Florida reports 485 cases through Oct 24, 2026, with 60 in week and one death.

triage.triage_reason: 本記事はデング熱の実際の流行報告ではなく、実験的抗ウイルス薬（モスノデンビル）の小規模臨床試験結果に関する研究報道であり、公衆衛生上の緊急性や異常性を示す感染症イベントではない。

article.articleHeadline: Nakhon Ratchasima reports a rabies outbreak; 48 animals infected, one death; accelerating the “Korat Model” to control the disease - Siam Rath
article.articleSummary: Rabies outbreak in Nakhon Ratchasima Province (Korat) with 48 infected animals identified, including 22 in Mueang District within a 5-km outbreak radius. A Feb 15, 2026 death occurred in a 54-year-old man who sustained dog bites and reportedly did not receive prior vaccination; clinical course led to rabies. In response, authorities launched expanded dog and cat sterilization and vaccination under the Korat Model, led by the Department of Livestock and local health agencies, at Phothi Klang Subdistrict and surrounding areas. Heart Dog Rescue and local partners have sterilized/vaccinated over 1,000 dogs; surveys indicate thousands more remain, with about 30% of dogs stray and some resident in military camps, parks, and public facilities. The strategy encompasses a broad 5-km radius, aiming to curb transmission to humans and animals, with MOUs to scale vaccination, sterilization, and surveillance across involved agencies.

article.articleHeadline: Ang Thong Prison screens sexually transmitted infections; 124 new inmates tested for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis C.
article.articleSummary: On November 12, 2026, Ang Thong Prison, in collaboration with the Prison Hospital of Ang Thong Province and the Medical Department staff of Ang Thong Hospital, launched HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis C screening for new male and female inmates. Blood-based testing was offered to 124 new arrivals during November 2569 (111 men and 13 women) to establish baseline health at intake, ensure access to medical services, and identify risks or abnormalities for timely treatment and follow-up. The initiative, part of the Prison Happiness program, aims to prevent and control communicable diseases within the prison, improve inmates' quality of life, and provide equitable health care. If infections are detected, detainees will enter appropriate care pathways. The effort underscores ongoing public health screening within correctional facilities in Ang Thong Province.

article.articleHeadline: New swine flu strain expected in Tatarstan — Vechernaya Kazan
article.articleSummary: In Tatarstan, Russia, the past week saw 7,116 infectious disease cases, a decline linked to school holidays. Health officials urge vaccination now, noting it takes up to two weeks to develop immunity. Currently 30 influenza cases have been confirmed, all H1N1. A new swine influenza strain, H3N2, is expected to enter circulation, with the main peak forecast for November–December and the season ending in March or April. Influenza activity is increasing even as noninfluenza etiologies predominate. Globally, Asia, the United States, and Europe report similar patterns, with no major outbreaks yet but some complications, including in Thailand. As a precaution, border testing for multiple diseases, including flu, is offered to travelers from Thailand; over 40 people have used this from two flights. Earlier vaccine-delivery delays are noted; the republic has received 1.6 million doses.

article.articleHeadline: Ghana Blood Donor Study Links Infection Risks to Geography and Donation
article.articleSummary: Six facilities in northern and Bono East Ghana (Wa Municipal, Tamale Central/West, SDA Tamale, Nkwanta South in Oti, Holy Family Hospital in Techiman) analyzed 3,348 blood donor records (Jan 2017–Dec 2022; 6,584 initially; 94.4% complete) to assess transfusion-transmissible infections. Overall infection prevalence was 14.78% across four targets: hepatitis B surface antigen 5.05%; syphilis antibodies 8.18%; hepatitis C antibodies 2.21%; HIV antibodies 0.72%. Syphilis was the most prevalent, and co-infections were rare (HBV+syphilis in 21; HBV+HCV in 8). Donor profile: predominantly men (91.2%), mean age 28.9 years; non-voluntary family replacement donations 94.5%, voluntary 5.5%; first-time donors 82% and repeat 18%. Laboratory screening used rapid diagnostic tests with HIV confirmatory testing; no nucleic acid testing or routine confirmatory treponemal assays. Risk with infections varied by donation history, geographic locality, and rural residence more than demographics, with logistic models applied separately per infection. Ongoing implication for targeted donor recruitment and screening in rural/semi-urban areas.

triage.notes: 本記事はガーナ北部・ボノ東部の献血者を対象とした後ろ向き研究(2017-2022年)で、HBV・HCV・梅毒・HIVの既知感染症の有病率を分析したもの。急性アウトブレイクや新規感染症イベントではないため、対象国リストに該当する発生国はあるが、トリアージ対象のシグナルとしては該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Ghana Malaria Surveillance Detects Artemether-Lumefantrine Resistance
article.articleSummary: Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) efficacy remains in Ghana as genomic surveillance of 764 Plasmodium falciparum isolates from Guinea Savannah, Forest, and Coastal zones (2010–2017) shows near-fixation of markers linked to artemether-lumefantrine tolerance, while validated pfk13 artemisinin-resistance mutations are absent. In the Forest zone, pfmdr1-N86 and the pfmdr1-N86F184D1246 haplotype reached 90–100% and 63.9–100% frequencies, reflecting divergent selective pressures: amodiaquine promotes 86Y/184Y/1246Y, whereas lumefantrine selects N86/184F/1246D. Across sites, Ghanaian samples included 400 dried-blood spots from asymptomatic children (2010–2014, Guinea Savannah), 200 hospital isolates (Begoro, Forest), and 164 (Ewim Polyclinic, Coastal) with high parasitemias; Savannah success was 25–73% due to low density, supplemented by HRM and PCR for pfmdr1, pfdhps, pfdhfr. The study used 128 P. falciparum loci plus a P. vivax marker, with 1000× depth. Globally, malaria caused ~282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024; ACTs remain functionally efficacious, though partner-drug pressure is emerging.

article.articleHeadline: Eastern Region targets 134,774 people for second round of river blindness treatment
article.articleSummary: River blindness (onchocerciasis) elimination drive: The Eastern Regional Health Directorate targets 134,774 people for the second round of the 2026 MDA from 15–28 November in four districts—Kwahu East, Kwahu Afram Plains North and South, and Ayensuano. The region's at-risk population is about 168,467 across 19 sub-districts and 366 communities. Nationwide, 15 regions and 86 districts aim to reach ~6.3 million. Ivermectin will be distributed house-to-house by trained health workers and Community-based Drug Distributors. Onchocerciasis is caused by Onchocerca volvulus and transmitted by blackflies around fast-flowing rivers; symptoms include itching, leopard skin, and blindness, making it the second-leading cause of avoidable blindness globally. MDA, health education, and community sensitisation are core strategies; exclusions include pregnant women, children under 90 cm tall, breastfeeding mothers with babies less than one week old, and seriously ill persons. Report adverse reactions to distributors or health facilities. Leaders urged to support participation.

article.articleHeadline: Senegal: Female genital schistosomiasis - The prevalence rate deemed 'concerning' in Richard-Toll and Podor
article.articleSummary: Female genital schistosomiasis prevalence in Senegal's Saint-Louis region is around 25% in the districts of Richard-Toll and Podor, a rate described as 'concerning' by regional Governor Al Hassan Sall. A meeting summarizing results of a study on the disease, a Neglected Tropical Disease, highlighted the burden in river-basin areas and urged community mobilization to control transmission. The study, conducted in Senegal with collaborations from Gaston-Berger University of Saint-Louis and Cheikh Anta Diop University of Dakar, is part of a broader multi-country effort including Mali, Ghana, Nigeria, and Madagascar. Dr Ndèye Mbacké Kane, coordinator of the National Program for Neglected Tropical Diseases, said authorities aim to sustain annual mass campaigns to reduce morbidity. The governor emphasized a need for a 'surge' to dominate and truly master schistosomiasis in the region.

article.articleHeadline: Screening detects latent tuberculosis infection in the Lao Cai - Cam Duong area
article.articleSummary: Latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) screening is underway in the Lao Cai–Cam Đường area, Vietnam, to detect latent infection and prevent progression to active TB. The provincial Center for Disease Control, with the Lao Cai–Cam Đường Regional Health Center and Hop Thanh Commune Health Station, organized screening on November 12–13, 2026, targeting 212 people. On November 12 at Hop Thanh, 52 close contacts of TB patients are screened; on November 13 at the regional center, 160 participants are tested. Priority groups include health workers, people with diabetes, dialysis patients, and those on long-term immunosuppressants, plus close contacts of pulmonary TB cases. Mantoux tuberculin skin tests are used; induration of 5 mm or more prompts chest X-ray to exclude active TB, and if lesions are suspicious, sputum GeneXpert is performed. LTBI is asymptomatic and non-contagious but may progress to active TB if immunity weakens; the program strengthens detection, management, and preventive therapy to reduce TB incidence toward elimination.
