article.articleHeadline: Study Identifies Twelve Avian Influenza Genotypes Circulating Across Laos
article.articleSummary: 37 H5 high-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses isolated in Laos from 2019 to 2024 show persistent circulation, extensive genetic diversity, and ongoing reassortment across three HA clades. Genotypes within clade 2.3.2.1e (E1–E7) predominated, while clade 2.3.4.4b (B1–B3) and clade 2.3.4.4h (H1–H2) were detected sporadically. A total of 12 genotypes were identified. Phylogenetic analyses indicate clade 2.3.2.1e genotypes co-circulated across Laos, Cambodia, and Vietnam; clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 in Laos (2023) clustered with viruses reported in East Asia and North America since 2021. Genotype H2 (clade 2.3.4.4h H5N6) is genetically similar to strains epidemiologically linked to a human infection in Laos and found in poultry and humans in China. Genotype E7 (2022–2024) shares the same constellation as viruses linked to human/mammalian infections in Cambodia and Vietnam. Findings highlight persistent H5 circulation and cross-border reassortment, underscoring the need for sustained genomic surveillance of transboundary and zoonotic risks in Southeast Asia.

article.articleHeadline: Asia-Pacific nations unite to launch plan to fight pandemics
article.articleSummary: Eight Asia-Pacific governments—Japan, Australia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines, Vietnam and Malaysia—launched an international framework in early October to counter future pandemics and bolster vaccine development, led by Japan’s Strategic Center of Biomedical Advanced Vaccine Research and Development for Preparedness and Response. The first meeting gathered infectious disease agencies from the eight nations and CEPI representatives to discuss disease prevalence and responses to threats such as dengue and Zika. The framework aims to coordinate strategies for vaccine development and diagnostic testing and to facilitate practical implementation across borders. A central goal is to urge CEPI to broaden funding for infectious disease control in Asia, addressing gaps when pathogens cross borders and remain undiagnosed due to sparse information sharing. Meetings will be held regularly on a rotating basis among the eight countries.

article.articleHeadline: Quang Ngai calls for vigorous, coordinated implementation of measures to prevent and control African swine fever.
article.articleSummary: Quang Ngai Province, Vietnam, on November 12, 2026, issued a plan to ramp up measures to prevent and control African swine fever (ASF), prioritizing early detection, rapid response, and strict enforcement against illicit pig movement and trade in pigs and pig products, with reinforced border controls with Laos. Since the start of 2026, ASF has affected 416 households across 37 communes and 116 villages in Quang Ngai, necessitating the culling of 3,043 pigs (about 146,052 kg) and causing substantial economic losses and environmental impact. Laos is experiencing a broad, complex ASF outbreak with limited containment, heightening the risk of cross-border spread to neighboring provinces including Quang Ngai. The plan assigns roles to agencies and local authorities, aims to eliminate outbreaks and ensure veterinary sanitary compliance, and to prevent illegal imports or smuggling of pigs.

article.articleHeadline: Rospotrebnadzor requested information about Russian tourists who were ill in Vietnam - Arguments of the Week
article.articleSummary: Rospotrebnadzor sought additional information after reports of illnesses among Russian tourists in Nha Trang, Vietnam. Symptoms were influenza-like: severe cough, runny nose, high fever, and headache. The agency sent a request to the Association of Tour Operators of Russia and prepared an official appeal to Vietnam’s Ministry of Health to obtain details on the current epidemiological situation, preventive measures, and traveler notification procedures. At this time, reports do not establish a single infection source or confirm an outbreak of a specific disease. Until official data are available, Russian authorities recommend standard protection against respiratory infections: frequent hand washing, avoiding close contact with sick individuals, and avoiding crowded places when possible. The development is particularly relevant for Russians planning travel to the popular resort of Nha Trang.

article.articleHeadline: Myanmar: Kachin begins second phase of measles and rubella vaccinations
article.articleSummary: As of 12 November 2026, Kachin State in Myanmar launched the second phase of the national measles and rubella vaccination campaign in Myitkyina, with Kachin State Governor U Khet Htein Nan leading the launch. He urged authorities and the public to inform families of vaccination locations and times and to identify and reach children who have not yet been vaccinated. The event marks continued efforts to boost coverage against measles and rubella within the state. No case counts or laboratory confirmations are reported in this brief, which centers on program rollout and community participation to improve immunization uptake.

article.articleHeadline: Cholera outbreak: WHO records more than 3,000 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Cholera outbreak: The World Health Organization reports more than 3,000 cholera deaths globally in the first nine months of 2026. Africa bears about 90% of fatalities, with six heavily affected regions: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Yemen, Zambia, Nigeria, Somalia, and Djibouti. The Democratic Republic of the Congo records the highest toll, with over 1,400 deaths, driven by limited access to safe water in coastal areas and refugee camps. Cholera, an acute diarrheal disease, is preventable and treatable with oral rehydration solution or intravenous fluids if addressed promptly before severe dehydration. Conflict and climate crises fuel spread; active war zones often lack medical action plans and infrastructure, while El Niño-fueled floods contaminate drinking water. WHO aims to cut cholera cases by 90% by 2030 after a global alliance approved 71 million doses of oral cholera vaccine, enabling mass campaigns that resumed after over three years.

article.articleHeadline: A California beach is closed after an E. coli outbreak leaves nine children ill.
article.articleSummary: Nine children in Santa Cruz County, California, have fallen ill with E. coli O157 linked to exposures at Capitola Beach and nearby waterways. Capitola Beach was temporarily closed on Nov 10, 2026, as the Santa Cruz County Health Services Agency investigates a possible common contamination source. Four of the cases live in Santa Cruz; the other five are from neighboring municipalities. The exact source remains unidentified; authorities believe exposure occurred at the beach or adjacent water bodies. E. coli O157 can cause gastroenteritis with diarrhea (sometimes bloody), abdominal cramps, and vomiting, with potential severe complications in young children. Environmental sampling has been conducted at four sites around the beach and Soquel Creek, including the lagoon, breakwater, and a channel linking the water to Monterey Bay, with additional testing planned.

article.articleHeadline: Soil monitoring after September Moss Landing fire | El Niño could bring more mosquitoes
article.articleSummary: Soil monitoring at Elkhorn Slough after September Moss Landing fire found no excess metals in inland soils, though metals were detected in harbor-area samples and soot coated boats on the ocean side. Recovery took nearly a year after the first fire, and data remain unmeasured due to capacity limits. Ivano Aiello of San Jose State University urged Monterey County to leverage Moss Landing Marine Labs in environmental-impact reviews, with no response yet. El Niño could worsen mosquito-season risk as rainfall and lingering floodwaters may boost West Nile virus transmission. Twenty-three California counties have reported West Nile cases this year; Monterey, Santa Cruz and San Benito counties have not. If floodwaters persist into spring/summer and temperatures rise, mosquito breeding could increase.

article.articleHeadline: Congenital syphilis cases in Bogotá already exceed the 2025 records: the most affected localities and what can be done to prevent the disease.
article.articleSummary: Congenital syphilis, caused by Treponema pallidum, rose in Bogotá, Colombia, in 2026. As of September 30, 2026 (preliminary), 90 congenital cases in newborns were notified, incidence 2.0 per 1,000 live births plus fetal deaths (NV+MF) based on 44,232 births/fetal losses. This contrasts with a sustained decline from 2020–2025 (315 in 2020; 203 in 2021; 177 in 2022; 115 in 2023; 103 in 2024; 75 in 2025). The nine-month 2026 figure exceeds 2025’s full-year total and remains above the PAHO/WHO elimination target of <0.5 per 1,000 NV+MF. Santa Fe district shows the highest incidence (6.9/1,000 NV+MF) with five cases; Ciudad Bolívar accounts for 19 cases (21.1%). Other high-notification localities include Engativá, Rafael Uribe Uribe, Usme, Suba, and Bosa. Of cases, 60 are Colombian and 30 foreign. The report advocates intensified maternal screening and treatment and public health actions such as the TIREMOS+CUIDADO initiative.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue fever and Chikungunya in Costa Rica
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever remains elevated in Costa Rica in 2026, with 6,594 cases recorded year-to-date, up 57% from 4,181 at the same point last year. Alajuela province leads with 2,791 dengue cases, followed by Puntarenas (981) and San José (880). Chikungunya totals reach 1,049 cases through mid-October, with the Chorotega health region (Guanacaste) contributing 602 cases, representing 57% of the national chikungunya total. La Cruz accounts for 389, Carrillo 90, and Santa Cruz 64. The data indicate concurrent transmission of dengue and chikungunya across multiple provinces, highlighting regional clustering and ongoing outbreaks in 2026 within Costa Rica. These figures come from the Costa Rica Ministry of Health.
